subject: System Design
title: Browser Caching
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Browser Caching.

hook.text: You visit a website twice. The second time, images load instantly. Your browser cached them locally.

buildup.text: Cache-Control headers tell browsers what to cache and for how long: max-age, no-cache, immutable.

discovery.text: Immutable assets with content hashes (app.abc123.js) can be cached forever — the hash changes on updates.

twist.text: Over-caching HTML pages can serve stale content for hours. HTML should use no-cache with ETags for revalidation.

climax.text: Browser caching is free performance. Proper Cache-Control headers can eliminate most repeat network requests.

punchline.text: Cache assets forever; revalidate HTML on every visit.

quiz.question: Why should immutable assets have long cache times?
options: Their content hash changes on updates, so stale versions are never served
